Simulate an Exponential Hawkes Process

Source: R/hsim.R
hsim.Rd

Simulate a univariate or multivariate path from an hspec-class specification, including marked and multi-kernel models.

Usage

hsim(
  object,
  size = 100,
  lambda_component0 = "auto",
  N0 = NULL,
  Nc0 = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'hspec'
hsim(
  object,
  size = 100,
  lambda_component0 = "auto",
  N0 = NULL,
  Nc0 = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

hspec-class. S4 object that specifies the parameter values.

size

Positive integer giving the number of output rows, including the initial state. At most size - 1 events are simulated.

lambda_component0

Initial intensity components \(\lambda_{ij}(0)\), excluding the baseline mu. A finite scalar is expanded to every kernel component. A matrix must match the shape of alpha and beta. The default "auto" (also NULL) uses unconditional component means for supported stable constant numeric linear models, and zero components otherwise. "mean" requires supported finite means; "zero" starts from baseline intensities. Selection is reported once, and zero initialization recommends supplying components explicitly. Other size adjustments are deprecated and produce a warning. Mean initialization excludes nonzero eta, impact callbacks and custom residual distributions. Function-valued core parameters use zero in "auto".

N0

Initial event counts: a finite scalar or one value per event type. The default is zero.

Nc0

Initial mark totals: a finite scalar or one value per event type. The default is zero.

verbose

Logical. Controls additional progress output; initialization selection is reported independently. Default is FALSE.

...

Further arguments passed to or from other methods.

Value

An S3 hreal object containing the simulated path, counting processes, and intensity components. If no further event can occur, the result contains only the generated rows and a warning reports the early termination. The initial row is included.

Details

The first row is the initial state. Its inter_arrival, type, and mark entries are zero; its N and Nc rows contain N0 and Nc0. Event types identify intensity rows. After a type i event, type_col_map[[i]] selects the kernel columns to update; without a mapping, column i is updated.

Simulation requires finite, nonnegative baselines. Signed kernel components are allowed when their sum is nonnegative and decreasing between events. For equal decay rates within a row, this requires a nonnegative row sum. For unequal rates, the simulator uses a sufficient condition: group components by decay rate, multiply each group sum by its rate, and check that cumulative sums in increasing rate order are nonnegative.

Simulation automatically uses an Rcpp event loop for plain numeric mu, alpha, and beta, including functions with exactly one param argument resolved to such values, and positive baselines in every dimension. This includes multivariate and mapped multi-kernel models with equal or unequal decay rates within a row. Equal-rate models use direct arrival sampling; unequal-rate models retain the R algorithm's thinning and rejected draws. Equal-rate models also support numeric eta, rmark functions requesting no event context, and impact functions requesting only lambda_component_n or no event context. Other optional arguments keep their defaults. Marks and impact components must be real numeric values. User functions still run in R; RNG state is synchronized before and after every call, including errors. Other event callbacks, ..., event-dependent baselines, custom residual distributions, zero baselines, and callback models with unequal rates use R. This selection is independent of emhawkes.engine, which controls likelihood calculations. Both paths use R's RNG in the same order. Arrival calculations use the current component state. Callbacks receive the arguments they request; callbacks with ... continue to receive the full supported context. Requesting full histories can increase copying costs for long paths.

To simulate an estimated model, use fitted_hspec() and pass fit_initial_state() to hsim() with do.call(). These arguments describe the start of the fitted observation window. Continuing after its last event requires the state at that event.

See also

fitted_hspec(), fit_initial_state(), logLik()

Examples


# example 1

mu <- 1; alpha <- 1; beta <- 2
h <- new("hspec", mu=mu, alpha=alpha, beta=beta)
hsim(h, size=100)
#> Initial intensity components: auto -> mean (unconditional component means).

# example 2
mu <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.1), nrow=2)
alpha <- matrix(c(0.2, 0.1, 0.1, 0.2), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
beta <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
h <- new("hspec", mu=mu, alpha=alpha, beta=beta)
res <- hsim(h, size=100)
#> Initial intensity components: auto -> mean (unconditional component means).
print(res)
